marker_alarm_joiner: The words that join two hours that share one later meridiem: "alarm for 7
marker_at_counts: Clock prepositions that also introduce a counted group: a bare hour behind one
is doubtful only right before a word of marker_counted_noun.voc.  Attested in
the parity acceptance rows; no dictionary source checked, a native reviewer is to confirm.
marker_clock_of: The clock suffix that ties a part of the day to an hour: "deux heures du
matin, dix heures du soir" (Larousse, "heure").  "le matin" without it is
the part of the day itself, so "réunion de deux heures le matin" is a length.
marker_counted_noun: Nouns that count people or things a clock never takes: a bare hour behind a
clock preposition and directly before one of them is a count ("wave at 5
people").  Each word is quoted from its Wiktionary Noun entry
(https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/<word>); the fetched pages are kept with the audit.
marker_date_article: The article that opens a weekday: "le mardi".  "Dans un texte suivi, on met
un déterminant défini devant le jour de la semaine et non devant la date"
(OQLF, Banque de dépannage linguistique, "Lieu et date dans la lettre",
section "Jour de la semaine devant la date").  Alone, "le mardi" is
also the habit; a habitual phrase reads as the next such day.
marker_defart: The definite article a date takes, and only that.  A French date is
masculine singular -- "le 15 juin", "le 1er janvier" -- so the feminine and
the plural are not dates and are not listed: "les" opens the recurrence
"tous les 10 mai", and an article slot that eats it takes the recurrence
marker_article.voc is the wrong slot here for a second reason.  It also
carries the contracted prepositions "du/des/au/aux", and a slot wide enough
to take those swallows the "du" of "la semaine du 20 juillet" -- the week OF
the twentieth, which then loses its week.
marker_half: clock/adjectival "demi/demie" plus period noun "moitié" (l'une des deux parties égales) -- TLFi/Larousse, s.v. "moitié".
marker_hour_approx: A word of approximation or of a start time before an hour.
vers: "À peu près (à telle époque). ➙ environ, sur. Vers (les) cinq
sur les: "(approximation) ➙ vers. Sur le soir." (Le Robert, s.v. "sur").
dès: "(temps) Immédiatement, à partir de." (Le Robert, s.v. "dès").
"pour" is not listed: the same entry gives a length too, "Pour six mois,
pendant six mois" (Le Robert, s.v. "pour"), so "je pars pour 3 heures" is
aux alentours de: "Aux alentours de (marque l'approximation). [...] ➙ vers."
marker_hour_statement: The verb that states the hour: "il est 3 heures", "c'est 3 heures", "il
était 3 heures".  "Il est une heure, midi, etc., sert à indiquer l'heure."
(Larousse, s.v. "être", Expressions avec être.)  "était" is the same verb.
The adverb "déjà" can stand between the verb and the hour: "déjà, adverbe.
Dès maintenant. [...] Il est déjà midi." (Le Robert, s.v. "déjà".)
marker_participle_aux: Forms of the auxiliary "avoir" (Larousse, conjugaison du verbe "avoir").
"été" right behind one is the past participle of "être" ("il a été",
"il avait été", "ils ont été", Larousse, conjugaison du verbe "être"), never the
season, which follows a determiner or a preposition ("l'été", "cet été", "en été").
marker_recur_habitual: Bare PLURAL definite article marking habitual weekday recurrence -- "les
lundis" ("on Mondays"), mirroring French's ordinary way of stating a
recurring weekday. Larousse/Grevisse: the plural article on a day-of-the-
week noun reads habitually, while the singular ("le lundi") is ambiguous
between "next Monday" and a habitual "on Mondays" and is deliberately
excluded from this vocabulary so only the unambiguous plural fires here.

unit_hour: "h" is the symbol of the hour: OQLF, Banque de dépannage linguistique,
"Écriture des nombres exprimant une durée": "2 heures 28 minutes (ou :
2 h 28 min)".  The fold reads "20h" as a clock elsewhere, so "h" reaches
this unit only after "dans" or "il y a".
After "dans" or "il y a", a count of hours and the minutes after it are one
length: "2 h 28 min" (OQLF, as above).  "et demie" adds half an hour: "Qui a
la valeur d'une moitié s'ajoutant à la quantité exprimée par le substantif.
Il a deux ans et demi" (TLFi, s.v. "demi", I.A).  "et quart" adds a quarter:
"Quart d'heure" : "Une des quatre parties égales d'une heure, quinze
minutes." (TLFi, s.v. "quart", B.1.a).  "moins" takes the minutes away:
"Pour indiquer une soustraction" (TLFi, s.v. "moins", II.A), so "dans 2 h
moins le quart" is a length of 1 h 45 min.
